chapter_title_en: The Trap in the Bamboo Grove
chapter_seo_title: Dao Gui Yi Xian Chapter 390: Sedan Chair Trap in the Infinite Bamboo Forest
chapter_meta_description: Li Huowang accepts a mysterious invite from a pale messenger—only to find himself trapped in an endless bamboo grove carried by inhuman bearers. Classic folk horror tension.
og_title: Dao Gui Yi Xian Ch. 390: The Bamboo Circle
og_description: A sedan chair, a silent bearer, and a two-hour ride to nowhere. Li Huowang learns not every invitation is what it seems.
twitter_title: Ch. 390 – Trapped in an Endless Bamboo Grove
twitter_description: Li Huowang’s divination leads him straight into a supernatural loop. No Zhuge Yuan in sight.

lore_anchors.definition: An ancient Chinese method of fortune-telling that interprets cracks or patterns on heated bones, especially scapulae or turtle plastrons. Here, Li Huowang uses his own arm bone, paying a visceral price for supernatural insight.
A small island setting in this chapter, named for its apricot trees. Likely a remote, liminal location where supernatural events occur.
Li Huowang’s signature weapon, a military-grade blade saturated with killing intent. It can cut both flesh and spirit, but its use carries a heavy psychological toll.
A common Chinese folk horror and xianxia trope where a vehicle or mount is used to lead a protagonist into a supernatural containment zone or ambush, often accompanied by a maze or time loop.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why does Li Huowang use his own bones for divination?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He can't find human bones on Apricot Island, so he uses his own arm bone. It reflects his willingness to sacrifice his body for the knowledge he needs.
The androgynous, powdered man claiming to be sent by Zhuge Yuan. His nature is deliberately ambiguous—likely a demon or spirit wearing a human guise.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why couldn't the sedan leave the bamboo grove?
cultural_notes_faq.a: The bearers were supernatural beings running in a loop, likely creating an illusion or containment array to trap Li Huowang.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Is Zhuge Yuan behind all this?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Very unlikely. The messenger is an impostor using Zhuge Yuan's name as bait, which is why Li Huowang attacks when he realizes the deception.
